articles.full_text:
France's extreme heat is creating an unusual problem for Champagne producers, with grapes ripening with higher-than-usual sugar levels and the permitted alcohol ceiling temporarily raised from 13% to 15% for this year's harvest.
The heatwaves, particularly in the Champagne region, have accelerated the ripening process of grapes on the vines.

South Africa’s wine sector heading for a sparkling 2026
As grapes ripen, their sugar levels increase.
During fermentation, that sugar is converted into alcohol.
With unusually high sugar levels in the grapes, the resulting Champagne could therefore have a higher alcohol content than usual.
French rules face an unusual challenge
There are particularly strict rules governing alcohol levels in France and the implications of grapes ripening under such extreme conditions.
The French authorities have temporarily increased the permitted alcohol ceiling for this year's Champagne harvest from 13% to 15%.
"It's fascinating that the world is changing and we're just going to have to move with it, right?" said Barbara Friedman of Primedia+.
Another speaker pointed to the wider implications of the change, asking what happens if the product no longer conforms to the strict requirements associated with Champagne.
"Big impact on the GNP," said CapeTalk presenter Clarence Ford.
A stronger Champagne?
The prospect of Champagne with a higher alcohol content also prompted a lighter reaction during the discussion.
One speaker joked about the implications of being able to drink less Champagne while achieving the same effect.
"They're going, ‘Oh, my goodness, I can have less of my Moët & Chandon, and I'll be as drunk," Friedman said.
The conversation also touched on the importance of appreciating Champagne rather than simply considering its alcohol content.
"A lot of fallout and implications" could result from the changes, Friedman said, noting that people will have to adapt as conditions change.
The discussion ultimately returned to the broader significance of what is happening in France: extreme heat is changing conditions in one of the world's best-known wine-producing regions, forcing established rules to adapt to an unusual harvest.

Watch: UAE man rescues injured gazelle from remote Dubai desert in scorching heat
- PUBLISHED: Tue 15 Sept 2026, 12:45 PM UPDATED: Tue 15 Sept 2026, 2:52 PM
For Mohammed Almehairbi, it was just another day of carrying on his father's legacy in the scorching UAE desert when he chanced upon an injured gazelle, trembling with fear.
The 47-year-old Emirati has been visiting Dubai's Saih Al Salam area — a rural desert spot — since 25 years, in memory of his father who used to hunt there for almost 50 years.
During his trips, he tends to the area, takes care of the animals and waters the plants, no matter the weather. On June 17, Almehairbi was roaming the area in his car when he spotted a gazelle in the middle of the desert.
Stay up to date with the latest news. Follow KT on WhatsApp Channels.
"It was not moving and was in the middle of the desert, which is very unusual, as gazelles are usually found resting under trees. I stopped at a distance because I didn't want it to run away," he said to Khaleej Times, after recently posting the video.
He continued to keep a 300-metre distance and waited until the injured animal fell asleep. "When it saw me, it started shaking and tried to run. I stayed away, otherwise it would have died trying to escape, especially in the extreme heat."
Once the situation was stable, Mohammed approached the animal and checked what was wrong and gave it some water. Soon after, he contacted the environmental department who rescued the gazelle and took it to a veterinary hospital.
Around 3 to 4 years of age, the gazelle had torn tendons and ligaments, making it difficult to sprint and move and was left in an extremely dehydrated state.
After receiving the apt medicines, treatments, and getting good care and food over the course of two weeks, the gazelle was released back into the same area.
"Since it is a male gazelle, we cannot release him anywhere else but the same area. Otherwise the male gazelles in other areas may get threatened and try to attack him."
A nature lover
A senior manager overlooking City Centre branches in the UAE, Almehairbi considers the desert his first home, especially after the passing of his father, who holds a special place in his heart.
The Saih Al Salam desert which he frequents on a weekly basis, is difficult to reach by car, yet he manages to go there with containers of water and food for the animals and plants in the surrounding area.
"There is a big lizard found in the desert called the Desert Monitor, I keep water for it. There are also some plants that have been there since my father's time and where he would take shade under; I keep watering them from time to time."
For the father of four, the rescue was not a favour he was doing for the animal, but a responsibility to the place that holds deep memories of his father for him.
What to do if you see animal in distress in UAE?
If you spot an injured animal in the UAE, ensure your safety first by keeping a distance, note the exact location, and immediately contact the local municipality or an animal rescue group such as the Dubai Municipality Animal Care and Welfare Centre at 800900 or the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment on 8003050.
While waiting at a safe distance, look out for fast traffic, sharp objects, or other immediate dangers that might cause harm to the animal or you. Due to the nature of the injured and scared animal, avoid feeding, giving water, or trying to treat wounds without professional training or help.
Always make sure to note the exact location, landmark, and the condition or number of animals before you call. If possible, take photos or videos, as proof can help authorities or rescue groups act faster.
Call on the following numbers in case of an emergency:
Dubai: Dubai Municipality - 800900
Abu Dhabi: Abu Dhabi Government contact center - 800 555; Wildlife Rescue programme - 800 500 054 for native wildlife; Abu Dhabi Animal Shelter - 02 8858100
Sharjah: Sharjah City Municipality - 993
Ajman: Municipality and Planning Department - 80070
Umm Al Quwain: Municipality of Umm Al Quwain - 06 764 1000
Ras Al Khaimah: Ras Al Khaimah Animal Welfare Centre - 07 2433184.
Fujairah: Fujairah Municipality - 80038
In case of any animal cruelty, residents must immediately reach out to the police at 999 across any emirate.
There also also many private organisations and local veterinary clinics that may help with rescuing and treating the animal.
Under UAE Federal Law No. 22 of 2016, private ownership, trading, or breeding of wild and dangerous animals is strictly banned. Violating this law by keeping an exotic pet or dangerous animal carries fines ranging from Dh10,000 to Dh500,000, plus potential jail time of up to six months.
Importance of gazelles in UAE culture
Gazelles are deeply important to the UAE as cultural symbols tied to national heritage, with the name Abu Dhabi literally translating to "Father of the Gazelle".
The Capital derives its name from a traditional legend where a wild gazelle guided early settlers to a fresh water source. The animal is also deeply rooted in the UAE's heritage, representing grace, speed, endurance, and deep-rooted survival in the harsh Arabian desert environment.
The Emirates is home to two native species of gazelles: the Arabian Gazelle, historically referred to as the mountain gazelle, and the Arabian Sand Gazelle, locally known as Al Reem.
Government initiatives managed by bodies like the Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi (EAD) utilise protected forests and islands, such as the Sir Bani Yas Island, to sustain tens of thousands of gazelles. Protected areas like the Dubai Desert Conservation Reserve and Al Ain Zoo are also known for being a haven for the vulnerable species.

articles.full_text:
Maraykanka ayaa xaqiijiyay inuu hawada sare, meeraha Dhulka ku wareegsan, geeyay hub loo adeegsado dagaalka hawada sare, taas oo ah markii ugu horreysay ee uu si rasmi ah u qiro inuu leeyahay awood noocaas ah oo weerar ah.
Xoghayaha Ciidanka Cirka ee Maraykanka, Troy Meink, ayaa sheegay in hubka ku sugan hawada sare uu muhiim u yahay ilaalinta ciidamada Maraykanka iyo ka hortagga weerarrada cadowga.
Isagoo Isniintii ka hadlayay shirkii Ciidanka Cirka, Hawada Sare iyo Internet-ka ee loo yaqaan Air, Space and Cyber Conference, Meink wuxuu sheegay in Maraykanku diyaar u yahay inuu wajaho "khataraha isbeddelaya", balse ma uusan faahfaahin awoodda hubkan ama xiligii hawada sare la geeyay.
Hoggaamiyeyaasha sare ee milatariga Maraykanka ayaa horey u sheegay inay qorsheynayaan in la xoojiyo awoodda milatari ee hawada sare, iyagoo tilmaamay barnaamijyada Ruushka iyo Shiinaha ee lagu horumarinayo habab lagu weerari karo ama lagu carqaladeyn karo dayax-gacmeedyada Maraykanka haddii uu mustaqbalka dagaal dhaco.
Maamulka Trump ayaa sheegay in awoodaha milatari ee hawada sare iyo gantaallada wax-ka-qabta ay qayb muhiim ah ka yihiin nidaamka difaaca uu qorsheeyay ee loo yaqaan "Golden Dome", kaas oo loogu talagalay in Maraykanka laga ilaaliyo gantaallada iyo khataraha kale ee hawada.
Heshiis caalami ah oo la saxiixay sannadkii 1967 ayaa mamnuucaya in hubka wax gumaada la geeyo ama lagu keydiyo hawada sare. Tan iyo markaas, quwadaha waaweyn oo ay ka mid yihiin Maraykanka, Ruushka iyo Shiinaha ayaa baarayay awoodo kale oo aan heshiiskaas si toos ah uga hor imaanayn, sida in la bartilmaameedsado dayax-gacmeedyada dalalka ay iska soo horjeedaan. Dayax-gacmeedyadu waxay muhiim u yihiin isgaarsiinta milatariga, la socodka iyo hagidda ciidamada.
Sannadkii hore, Madaxweyne Donald Trump wuxuu soo saaray amar fulineed oo xoojinaya doorka Ciidanka Hawada Sare ee Maraykanka , isaga oo sheegay in ciidanku uusan ku koobnaan doonin oo keliya difaaca hantida Maraykanka ee hawada sare, balse uu sidoo kale yeelan karo awood weerar.
US Space Force, oo ah laanta ugu cusub ee ciidamada qalabka sida ee Maraykanka muddo ka badan 70 sano, waxaa la aas-aasay sannadkii 2019 si loo ilaaliyo hantida Maraykanka ee hawada sare, oo ay ku jiraan boqolaal dayax-gacmeed oo loo adeegsado isgaarsiinta iyo kormeerka.
Warbixinada qotada dheer iyo wararka BBC Somali oo toos kuugu imanaaya WhatsApp.
Halkaan kaga soo biir
Dhamaadka xayeysiinta
Afhayeen u hadlay Ciidanka Hawada Sare ee Maraykanka ayaa sheegay in "xakamaynta hawada sare" ay ka kooban tahay hawlgallada looga baahan yahay in lagu tartamo laguna xakameeyo goobta hawada sare, iyadoo la adeegsanayo habab waxyeello geysta iyo kuwo aan waxyeello toos ah geysan si loo carqaladeeyo, loo wiiqo ama xitaa loo burburiyo awoodaha cadowga haddii loo baahdo.
Afhayeenku wuxuu sheegay in awoodahan loo adeegsan karo difaac iyo weerarba, iyadoo lagu salaynayo amarrada hoggaanka ciidamada dagaalka.
Horraantii bishii Febraayo, waxaa la shaaciyay in laba dayax-gacmeed oo Ruushku leeyahay ay u badan tahay inay qabteen ama dhexgaleen isgaarsiinta ugu yaraan 12 dayax-gacmeed oo Yurub leeyahay tan iyo markii Ruushku duullaanka ku qaaday Ukraine sannadkii 2022-kii.
Dhexgalka noocaas ah ayaa laga yaabaa inuu sirdoonka Ruushka u saamaxay inuu akhriyo xogta xasaasiga ah ee ay dayax-gacmeedyadu gudbinayeen, ama, aragti ahaan, xitaa inuu la wareego gacan-ku-haynta dayax-gacmeedyada.
Sannadkii 2024, Maraykanku wuxuu sheegay in Ruushku hawada sare u diray dayax-gacmeed uu Maraykanku aaminsanaa inuu awood u leeyahay inuu weeraro dayax-gacmeedyo kale. Ruushku si rasmi ah ugama uusan hadlin arrintaas.
Ciidanka Hawada Sare ee Maraykanka ayaa sheegay in Shiinuhu "horumariyo oo isticmaalo awoodo hawada sare iyo kuwa lidka-hawada sare ah, taas oo qayb ka ah istaraatiijiyaddiisa casriyeynta milatariga."
Waxa kale oo uu sheegay in Ruushku "hawada sare u arko goob dagaal, isla markaana aaminsan yahay in ka sarreysnaanta hawada sare ay noqon doonto arrin go'aamisa dagaallada mustaqbalka."

articles.full_text:
Paris artist reveals heatwave’s devastating impact on homeless in stark drawings
Paris has been grappling with intense heat and illustrator Marina Antonova captures this in her series ‘Chronicles of a Heating Planet’
- Bookmark
Jump to contentParis artist reveals heatwave’s devastating impact on homeless in stark drawings
As Paris transitions into the cooler temperatures of autumn following months of intense heat, the memory of France’s hottest summer on record remains vivid — preserved in the work of illustrator Marina Antonova.
While the French capital is globally renowned for its architectural and aesthetic charm, the city repeatedly featured in international news as record-breaking temperatures rose beyond 40C (104F) on its sun-baked streets.
In a collection of illustrations titled "Chronicles of a Heating Planet", Antonova has depicted a city under acute heat stress, highlighting the impact on the homeless population in particular.
"The heat wave made it so much worse," Antonova told The Associated Press in a recent interview at the Paris apartment where she drew much of her work. "Usually winter is the hardest part for homeless people; now we have a situation where both winter and summer are horrific."
Her drawings portray rough sleepers hunched forward in despair, clutching their knees, or collapsed on pavements.
"It was such a contrast, people working in posh air-conditioned offices and homeless people sleeping in front of those offices," Antonova, 37, said. "I cannot imagine how people survived."
Since relocating to France from Russia four years ago, Antonova has moved between temporary accommodation. Despite support from friends, she frequently endured poor living conditions, mental strain, and limited financial resources.
The intense suffering of those living on the streets resonated with her, leaving her distressed by an inability to provide further help.
While extra blankets can offer warmth during winter, relieving body heat during periods of extremely high daytime and night-time temperatures presents a different challenge. "You bring them water and ice but it never stops," said Antonova, who reflected the aggression of an unyielding sun through her choice of palette.
"In my images there is a lot of yellow, an acid color," Antonova said. "Usually you associate the sun with something nice, this year it was very different for everyone. It felt very aggressive and dangerous, there were also fires around the country."
Other works in the collection show animals disorientated inside burning forests, with deer running directly towards fires as escape routes disappear.
"What happens to beauty when the landscape itself turns hostile?" Antonova asks. "Wildfires burned across southern Europe and then — in a place long thought safe from them — at the edge of Paris itself. In July, fire swept through the forest of Fontainebleau."
Unprecedented fires also destroyed vast areas of forest near Bordeaux, forcing thousands of residents from their homes. Countries across Europe, including Italy and Spain, recorded extreme heat on a continent recognised as the fastest-warming in the world.
During successive heatwaves this year, France registered at least 7,200 more deaths than expected, according to estimates by the national public health agency using statistical models based on historical data.
"Chronicles of a Heating Planet" examines the reality of daily life when climate change shifts from a future forecast to an ongoing condition.
"These paintings are not illustrations of a single event," added Antonova, who began drawing as a child. "They are observations of a future that has already arrived."
As extreme temperatures severely affected daily life, navigating Paris in the sun became increasingly difficult.
"I have an artist friend who still lives in Russia. When I sent her my new drawings of Paris, she said ‘Oh thank you, I will never go to Paris after this,’" Antonova said. "We called this series ‘anti-postcards.' The kind of postcards where you don't want to go to the place. It's a kind of sad joke."
The series prompts questions about whether recurring heatwaves might eventually deter visitors from standing in long queues at the city's popular landmarks. "In five or 10 years Paris could get so hot people might not want to go here, not in summer, anyway," Antonova suggested.
"My series about the heat wave gave me the opportunity to look at very familiar places with a new angle," she added. "To rethink the tourist attractions in a more sinister and dangerous atmosphere."
Antonova created the digital illustrations on an iPad, using photos taken on her mobile phone across various parts of the city.
"Since I became an immigrant it was difficult to organize studios every time I moved, so I started working more with digital illustration," she explained.
"Usually I wouldn’t do drawings about something on the news because I would need a longer time to process and create the painting. Ipad gives you the immediacy because it’s so much faster."

articles.title: Fime targets digital trust as it snaps up Red Alert Labs - FinTech Global
articles.search_term: ("heat advisory" OR "heat action plan" OR "heat alert" OR "IMD warning" OR "IMD alert" OR "red alert" OR "orange alert" OR "yellow alert" OR "NDMA advisory" OR "cooling shelter" OR "relief measures" OR "heat compensation" OR "severe weather warning") Assam
articles.full_text:
Fime has acquired Red Alert Labs, an accredited cybersecurity evaluation, certification and compliance automation specialist, as part of its push to widen its assurance offering.
The deal brings cybersecurity evaluation, certification expertise and compliance automation into Fime’s existing capabilities, adding a new pillar to a business that has so far concentrated on payments, smart mobility and digital identity.
Central to the acquisition is Red Alert Labs’ CyberPass platform, which automates compliance work: alongside accredited security evaluation, it lets manufacturers assess and continually improve their readiness, while giving certification schemes a way to manage and scale assessment and certification processes.
Fime frames the acquisition as a response to digital ecosystems becoming more interconnected, meaning trust can no longer be handled in isolated pockets.
Payments, digital identities, connected devices and AI-enabled services are converging around common requirements: security, interoperability, compliance and proof that technologies keep working as intended over time.
The company’s stated ambition is to build the trust infrastructure that lets these ecosystems scale, drawing on combined expertise, testing and assurance platforms, and independent evaluation and certification across a product’s lifecycle.
Timing is a factor too. New cybersecurity rules are landing this year, with Cyber Resilience Act reporting obligations applying from 11 September 2026 and the Act’s main obligations following on 11 December 2027.
That regulatory shift means manufacturers will need to prove cybersecurity compliance on an ongoing basis, not only when a product first launches, which is where Fime sees Red Alert Labs’ continuous-assurance approach adding value.
Fime has built its reputation over three decades primarily in payments testing and certification, later extending into digital identity and smart mobility. With this acquisition, the two companies plan to support customers across the full lifecycle: advisory work and security by design, through implementation, testing, evaluation and certification, and on into continuous assurance, bringing cybersecurity under the same umbrella as its existing payments and identity work.
Red Alert Labs will keep operating as an accredited, independent cybersecurity laboratory, retaining the accreditations and technical autonomy it has built its name on. It will now trade under the identity “Red Alert Labs, cybersecurity by Fime”, pairing its security expertise and technology with Fime’s international reach and testing infrastructure.
Fime CEO Lionel Grosclaude said, “Our ambition is to make Fime a global Digital Trust Provider. For more than three decades, we have helped build trust in payments, and we have extended that expertise into digital identity and smart mobility. Cybersecurity is the next natural step.
“These markets are converging: customers increasingly need to prove not only that a product works and interoperates, but that it is secure, compliant and remains trustworthy throughout its lifecycle. Red Alert Labs brings us world-class cybersecurity expertise together with a platform approach that will help us deliver that trust at scale.”
Red Alert Labs founder and managing director Roland Atoui said, “Red Alert Labs was built around the idea that cybersecurity assurance needs to become scalable and continuous.
“Joining Fime gives us the opportunity to combine our accredited evaluation expertise and CyberPass platform with Fime’s global testing, certification and digital trust capabilities. Together, we can help manufacturers continuously assess their compliance readiness, help schemes industrialize certification, and extend cybersecurity trust into digital identity, wallets and emerging agentic ecosystems.”

articles.full_text:
THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast rain across Kerala over the next five days and issued yellow alerts for several districts. A yellow alert is in place in Malappuram, Kozhikode and Wayanad on Tuesday, with isolated heavy rainfall expected. Heavy rain refers to rainfall between 64.5 mm and 115.5 mm in 24 hours.
Yellow alert
September 16: Pathanamthitta, Idukki and Ernakulam
September 19: Pathanamthitta and Idukki
Isolated heavy rain is likely in Kerala on September 15, 16, 19, 20 and 21. Thunderstorms accompanied by rain and strong winds reaching 40–50 kmph are also likely in isolated places on September 15 and 16. The IMD has also forecast thunderstorms in isolated parts of the state on September 17, 18 and 19.
Kallakkadal warning
The National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) has warned of the possibility of coastal flooding due to high waves associated with the Kallakkadal phenomenon.
Waves reaching 0.7 to 1.1 metres are likely along the coasts of Thiruvananthapuram, from Kappil to Pozhiyoor; Kollam, from Alappad to Edava; Kozhikode, from Chombala to Ramanattukara; and Kannur, from Valapattanam to New Mahe, until 11.30 pm on September 16.
Fishermen and coastal residents have been advised to remain alert due to the possibility of rough sea conditions.
People living in vulnerable areas have been advised to move to safer locations as directed by the authorities.
The use of small boats and fishing vessels should be avoided during this period.
Bringing fishing vessels back to shore can be as dangerous as taking them out to sea when the Kallakkadal phenomenon and high waves are expected. Fishing vessels should therefore not be launched or brought ashore when the waves intensify.
All beach-related activities, including tourism, should be completely avoided until the INCOIS warning is withdrawn.
Fishing vessels such as boats and canoes should be securely moored at harbours, with adequate distance maintained between vessels to prevent collisions. Fishing equipment should also be kept secure.
People have also been advised to avoid trips to beaches and all recreational activities in the sea.

Kutch's Mandvi inundated after 5 inches of rain:Markets flooded, rivers overflowing; red alert in 6 districts including Diu
Rainfall was recorded in 42 talukas between 6 am and 10 am today (15 Sept). Mandvi in Kutch received 5 inches of rain in the last two hours, causing severe waterlogging.
The Meteorological Department has issued a red alert for Kutch, Dwarka, Jamnagar, Porbandar, Junagadh, Gir Somnath and Diu until 1 pm, warning of heavy to extremely heavy rain.
An orange alert has been issued for Rajkot, Morbi and Amreli, while other districts remain under a yellow alert for light to moderate rainfall.
259 talukas receive rain in 24 hours
The second spell of monsoon rain, which began across the state on September 12, has remained intense. Rainfall was recorded in 259 talukas over the past 24 hours.
Anjar in Kutch received the highest 7.24 inches, followed by 6.10 inches in Vallabhipur, Bhavnagar.
More than 4 inches of rain was recorded in 14 talukas, while 26 talukas received over 3 inches. Other talukas recorded rainfall ranging from 1 mm to 3 inches. Gujarat has received 84.38% of its average seasonal rainfall so far, leaving a 15.62% deficit.
Water flowed like a river in Mandvi, see the pictures.
Heavy rain at start of Bhadarv brings relief after dry Shravan
The rainfall expected during Shravan was largely absent this year. However, the spell of heavy rain at the beginning of Bhadarv has brought relief to farmers and the government.
Despite significant rainfall over the past three days, the state is still facing a 17% deficit against its average rainfall. Gujarat has received 80% of its average seasonal rainfall so far, but concerns remain over the rainfall situation in Saurashtra and Kutch.
Narmada reservoir crosses 95% storage, but 79 dams remain below 25%
Water storage in the Narmada reservoir has crossed 95% of its capacity. However, the other 206 reservoirs across the state have recorded only 67% storage so far. As many as 79 dams still have less than 25% of their storage capacity filled.
Scenes of the devastation caused by yesterday’s rainfall in Ahmedabad.
Saurashtra under yellow alert as monsoon remains active
The monsoon remains active over Gujarat due to an active system, trough, low-pressure system, monsoon trough and western disturbance. Several districts in Saurashtra and Kutch are under a yellow alert for heavy rain today.
Rain intensity likely to ease from September 16
Ahmedabad is expected to remain generally cloudy today, with chances of heavy showers. However, rainfall intensity is likely to decrease from September 16, with light to moderate showers expected across most areas. Fishermen and residents of low-lying areas have been advised to remain cautious.

articles.title: Heat-related damage to the LVB rail network in 2026: A heat action plan is intended to help, but a radical overhaul is needed - Leipziger Zeitung

In June, the joint sealant melted along 36 kilometres of the Leipzig Public Transport Authority (LVB) track network. Tram services came to a complete standstill for days, and 2,000 Leipzig residents rushed to help when the LVB sought volunteers to scrape away the overflowing joint sealant. In some cases, they did so even when temperatures were well over 30 degrees. For the first time, the LVB also experienced what the new ‘record temperatures’ mean for Leipzig. And, naturally, a great many passengers wondered: Will lessons be learnt from this? Will anything change now?
On Monday 14 September, TÜV SÜD Rail and the LVB presented a final report on these instances of liquefaction in the track network. The aim, of course, is to prevent such damage in future and to make the infrastructure more climate-resilient for the future. The latter, however, remains a completely open question even after this presentation.
The first warning shot
At the end of June, around 36 kilometres of the LVB’s track network were contaminated by bitumen in the joints that had liquefied, forcing services to be suspended. And somehow, the heat was to blame. And it was. It was a warning sign, as peak temperatures of 40 degrees and above will characterise future summers in Leipzig. However, the tram track network is not designed to cope with this.
The German Weather Service recorded the second-hottest summer since records began, including a doubling of the number of hot days with tropical nights. In Leipzig, the hottest day on record – with temperatures exceeding 40 degrees – was recorded on 27 June 2026. And that was precisely the day when the bitumen problem brought Leipzig’s trams to a standstill. Although the problem did not start with the bitumen. On the tracks and joints alone, the LVB recorded temperatures of more than 70 degrees.
The sections where the bitumen liquefied were generally located on large, open stretches of road without any shade, mainly around the ring road, where – in addition to unobstructed sunlight – heat also tends to build up particularly.
It is precisely the vast traffic areas that were cleared around the Ring back in GDR times that form the most intense heat hotspots in the city centre. Anyone who waited at a tram stop there during the hot weeks knows what that meant. And what a shock it was to then board trams where the air conditioning was completely overwhelmed. Sweat-inducing temperatures both inside and out.
4.5 million euros in damage
According to the LVB, this caused damage to infrastructure and trams in Leipzig amounting to up to 4.5 million euros. Other European cities, such as Budapest, Nuremberg and Essen, also suffered significant damage and disruption for passengers. We were not alone in this predicament.
Gradually, thanks to the efforts of nearly 2,000 people who cleaned the tracks, the full service schedule was restored in July. A provisional heat plan was also drawn up straight away to ensure that a similar collapse would not occur again during the next hot weeks.
“With this TÜV report, we now want to further underpin the LVB heat plan we have developed in order to prevent future damage and continue to operate a climate-resilient infrastructure going forward. In view of the predicted climate changes, this is a task for society as a whole,” said Toralf Müller, Managing Director of Technology and Operations at Leipziger Verkehrsbetriebe, on Monday.
The inspection results
TÜV SÜD Rail carried out investigations on behalf of LVB and, amongst other things, conducted a visual survey of the current condition and damage to joints dating from various decades and constructed by different building contractors. The affected track sections were inspected and samples of the joint compound were taken.
This was because it was not entirely clear why the compound had liquefied in some sections but remained unaffected in others. In addition, documents from the planning and construction files were examined, and the bituminous joint compound used was analysed in the laboratory.
The final report now shows – unsurprisingly – that there was no single cause of the heat damage, but rather that a combination of various factors played a part. LVB summarises it as follows: “The record-breaking heat, with consistently tropical temperatures over several days, combined with the strain on the tracks caused by car, lorry and bus traffic, resulted in significant damage that led to the suspension of services.”
The buses pulling into bus stops during the record-breaking temperatures dislodged the already molten material from the joints with their tyres. Similar effects were observed at major junctions, which were baking in the heat.
The planning failures of the last century
It’s clear that the city, too, must finally change its approach. For years, Leipzig’s environmental organisations have been calling for a reduction in the number of lanes around the ring road and a downsizing of the completely oversized junctions, such as the one at Goerdelerring. The fact that this could also be important in the face of increasingly frequent heatwaves became apparent for the first time in this way this year. The liquefaction of the joint sealant is the result of such flawed road planning from the last century.
And what can be done about it now?
With regard to the requirements for longitudinal track joints, TÜV SÜD Rail continues to recommend the use of bituminous joint sealant, as well as quality assurance through close monitoring during construction and installation, and adjustments to ensure a climate-resilient infrastructure. For example, the joints should be installed lower beneath the rail head.
The addition of plastic granules to the joint compound to prevent adhesion to tyres and wheels is currently still being investigated. This is because it is significantly more expensive. A real problem in times of tight budgets.
“No single contributing factor could be identified as the cause of the damage observed. The findings suggest a combination of various factors. The prolonged heatwave is considered a key contributing factor. At the same time, there is scope for further improvement in the installation documentation,” said Ian Veigl, Inspector and Lead Auditor at TÜV Süd Rail.
The heat problem caused by vast sealed surfaces
Of course, the LVB cannot change the ‘historical’ framework created by the generous road cross-sections. But it also became clear that the joint sealant problem is linked to the continuous sealing of the track beds. The LVB should really also be considering extensive unsealing of the paved sections – particularly wherever buses do not need to use the track. Green tracks on the Ring would actually be a logical conclusion.
In other words: the LVB really needs to rethink its approach, particularly around the Ring.
At present, there is very little they can do. The findings of the TÜV investigation are now being incorporated into the LVB’s principles for climate-resilient construction and infrastructure design, as well as into the LVB’s heat plan. The two-stage plan provides for various measures at 33 and 38 degrees respectively, covering monitoring, cooling and, if necessary, the closure of individual routes. The heat plan was already put into action in July and proved its worth, according to the LVB. Cooling can be achieved – as was even practised in GDR times – using water sprinkler lorries.
“It was only thanks to the tremendous commitment of the people of Leipzig, our colleagues at the transport company and the Leipzig Group that we were able to gradually resume services. A heartfelt thank you to everyone who helped. We will continue to systematically address the effects of climate change on our infrastructure, exchange ideas within the industry and work with experts from universities, planning offices and construction firms to develop solutions that meet our requirements,” emphasised Stefan Röll, Head of Infrastructure at Leipziger Verkehrsbetriebe.
The majority of the damaged joints on the LVB network are due to be repaired by the end of the year. According to the LVB, this may result in further short-term closures.
